title: Cat50: Shot-Zone Aggregated Statistics (CPU-Compatible Shot-Chart Embeddings)
source: MDPI 2026 paper — Uncertainty-Aware Machine Learning for NBA Forecasting (doi:10.3390/info17010056)
motivation: The 2026 MDPI paper achieved Brier 0.199 using spatial shot-chart embeddings (CNN 48x48 heatmap → 128-dim → PCA 20). Our CPU-only constraint rules out CNN, but we can approximate the signal with zone aggregations — splitting the court into 7 canonical zones (restricted area, paint non-RA, mid-range, corner 3, above-break 3, at-rim, free-throw) and computing per-zone FGA, FG%, frequency, and relative efficiency. This is pure arithmetic over existing shot data — no GPU needed.

implementation.data_source: NBA Stats API play-by-play / shot chart detail (already fetched in Cat34-Cat36)

expected_impact.brier_delta: -0.003 to -0.008 based on literature ablations showing each modality contributes unique signal
expected_impact.confidence: MEDIUM — CPU aggregations capture 60-70% of CNN spatial signal per ablation study
expected_impact.roi_impact: POSITIVE — shot quality differential is forward-looking for in-game efficiency

risks: Shot chart data availability varies by season (pre-2015 incomplete)
Zone definitions must match NBA Stats API zones exactly to avoid noise
May overlap with existing Cat34-Cat36 (shooting efficiency) — run SHAP correlation check before deploying
action: Implement compute_cat50_shot_zones in features/engine.py. Add to engine init. Version bump to v3.1-47cat. Deploy to all 6 islands via hf-space sync.
next_step: Run features/engine.py test to verify Cat50 outputs on 2024-25 season sample. Cross-ref with Cat34-Cat36 via SHAP to confirm low redundancy.
